title: Number the devices
prompt: A churn model needs each member's preferred device as a number. Write `solve(users)` so it returns `user_id`, `preferred_device` and `device_index`, numbering the devices by how many members use them.
rules: The most common device gets 0.0, the next 1.0, and so on. Devices used by the same number of members are numbered alphabetically.
A member with no `preferred_device` gets the number after the last device. Missing values don't count as a device.
Return `user_id`, `preferred_device` and `device_index` (a double), in that order. Keep every member.
hints: `StringIndexer` numbers values by frequency, most frequent first, and breaks ties alphabetically.
By default it stops on a missing value. Which `handleInvalid` setting gives missing values an extra index instead of dropping the row?
`fit` the indexer on `users`, `transform` the same DataFrame, then `select` the three columns.
